source.section: TC-40 lines 4 to 22 (Instructions PDF p.9 Line 4; PDF p.10 Lines 5 to 20 and the Line 17 table; PDF p.11 Line 22); Line 21 and Qualified Exempt Taxpayer Worksheet lines 1 to 5 (PDF pp.10-11); (57) Municipal Bond Interest (PDF p.18); (71) Utah Municipal Bonds (PDF p.19)

worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = wages (person 0) 23,625.00 = 23,625.00. Federal taxable income = 23,625.00 - standard deduction 23,625.00 = 0.00 (federal senior deduction ignored; Utah starts from federal AGI). TC-40 (head of household): line 4 federal AGI 23,625.00. Line 5 additions: code 57 municipal interest from other states 30,000.00, 30,000.00. Line 6 = 23,625.00 + 30,000.00 = 53,625.00. Line 7 state tax refund 0.00. The other-state bonds were bought after Jan. 1, 2003 from a state that taxes interest on Utah's bonds, so code 57 applies. Line 8 subtractions 0.00. Line 9 Utah taxable income = 53,625.00 - 0.00 - 0.00 = 53,625.00. Line 10 = 53,625.00 x 0.045 = 2,413.13. Lines 11 to 16, by the projection: no dependents; the deduction on line 12 is held as the cap 23,625.00; initial credit = 0.06 x min(line 9 53,625.00, cap 23,625.00) = 0.06 x 23,625.00 = 1,417.50. Line 17 base phase-out amount 27,320.00. Line 18 = max(0, 53,625.00 - 27,320.00) = 26,305.00. Line 19 = 26,305.00 x 0.013 = 341.965. Line 20 = max(0, 1,417.50 - 341.965) = 1,075.535. Line 21 worksheet: line 1 federal AGI 23,625.00; line 2 standard deduction 23,625.00; line 3 senior deduction 0.00 (no amount in Utah's sources); line 4 23,625.00; line 5 = max(0, 23,625.00 - 23,625.00) = 0.00. Line 5 is zero, so the filer is exempt: X on line 21 and 0 on line 22 (the form still shows lines 9 and 10 as above). In the expected lines exempt_in_full takes the whole of line 9, 53,625.00, off state income, so state_agi and taxable income are 0.00, and with them the tax and the credits; no credit is claimed. At the head of household threshold the relief stays.
